title: Rigged models effected by light, rendering with black spots
body:
### Tested versions

4.2 stable

### System information

Mobile, Compability, Vulkan, Android

### Issue description

I worked on a simple scene with a bit of 3D, rigged animated characters (.GLB format), and lighting. While testing on my Windows 10 computer or exporting to my Google Pixel 7 Pro, everything was fine. However, when I decided to check the same export on a Google Pixel 5 and a Realme 6 Pro, these black spots appeared on the characters. 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/106619492/1db76758-0043-4408-a24d-d4a4f0e2a718


I tested in both mobile and compatibility renderers, and the spots were only on the characters. I found the cause of this issue: whenever there's any node in the scene that is a child of Light3D and this light affects the mesh, the spots appear. In the scene, there's only the standard WorldEnvironment and standard DirectionalLight3D (sun), which are added by default in the editor (just added it with the 3-dots menu). When I disabled the DirectionalLight3D node, the spots disappeared. I tried all the node settings, but nothing helped. There's also a good example where it's evident that as soon as the characters get close to the light source, the spots appear, and as soon as they move out of its range, the spots vanish.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/106619492/4f2d972c-ee63-4cba-8919-991f0564617b

Additionally, I found a similar case on the forum, but there is no solution provided there. : https://godotforums.org/d/35859-lights-on-android-export

### Steps to reproduce

Something tells me that this issue is straightforward, and what I've written is enough to pinpoint the problem. If not, and if this case turns out to be interesting, I will detail everything about the issue, test it multiple times, and send a Minimal Reproduction Project.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

**Bugsquad edit**: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/15045972/TEST.zip

Hey @participant3! :)  I believe a recent update to Godot may be significantly exasperating the issue as it appears in several of our models now on our Android devices where previously we had not noticed.  Both our Samsung and Google Pixels are experiencing this.

Here are some pictures demonstrating what we are seeing:

**Android**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b81375a-8db2-499b-948d-a2e21a21efc3)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e63daf5a-ce77-4680-8fc3-ee08a76a072a)

**Linux Desktop**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/748bcea1-5882-4d7d-935d-0393804c6689)


Pretty much everything you see that is black is an artifact that ONLY appears on our Android devices.  Linux, Windows, iOS, Mac, all work just fine.  There are some super interesting things to point out in these pictures:

1. The black artifacts.  But of course we already know about that.
2. The pictures / icons on the left.  Those are taken at runtime, offscreen, through a viewport that isn't displayed to the user, so that we can generate inventory icons at runtime.  Interestingly, these black artifacts don't seem to appear there for some reason.
3. Check out this next picture:

In a separate scene, the dragons render just fine without artifacts:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e4192f4-3627-4e27-a2fb-47b30bd799fb)

I do not yet know what is causing causing this.  And I can't find a workaround.  Some scenes have issues.  Others do not.

> Any updates will be posted here. It seems no one is actively working on this, so I wouldn't expect to see any updates in the immediate future.

I'm not sure how issues are prioritized in Godot.  And I don't want to apply any undo pressure as I know this is mostly developed by volunteers such as all of us here alongside _some_ full time devs through donations.  However, may it be possible to increase priority on this issue?  Android devices hold a HUGE market share in the mobile world and I would like to not have to offer our Android users a degraded experience.

Thank you again for all of the hard work!  Please let me know if there is anyway I can help further this along :)

@participant2 @participant4 Okay I figured out how to do it for glb files.  You need to open it with blender and then export without normals enabled:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e8823f1-5a92-4257-87aa-e28765d44185)

I presume Godot then does normal calculations on the model.  ~However, that seems to come with its own issues:~

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93b4446b-1481-4e19-be6d-fc041c48f529)

~As can be seen, the lighting here is resulting in hard shadows rather than a smooth blend across the vertices like it was before with its previous normals:~

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19ecb21-4dc0-4c7f-8ede-f4601e837008)

I take that back.  Even the previous normals resulted in this hard line.  Maybe its just too low poly.  Fortunately for my very specific use case, users will never see the back side of this model.  So I can shade the front side and call it a day :)

I'm going to test not exporting normals from blender with my other problematic models and see what happens.

NOTE:

I do not like this solution though.  It means I cannot edit the normals of my models and I have to rely on Godot's normals generation.  Which I expect will not always give the results I want.  I hope this acts as a decent enough workaround for my current models and I will soon find out.  I still stand by what I said above though where I believe this should be a higher priority issue if anyone with the knowledge on how to fix it has the capacity to do so.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
This might be the same issue as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86275. I am testing out the precision change now. 

_edit: The suggested changes from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86275 are sufficient to fix this PR._

I think I understand the issue now. This particular model is huge, so it uses a transform of 0.01 to scale the mesh down. However, that also scales the normal. So the normal ends up being extremely small before being interpolated (~0.005) since interpolation happens with only half floats, this results in the normal breaking. 

Accordingly, there are two solutions:
1. Interpolate in highp (full precision)
2. normalize the normal before interpolation so it is in a reasonable range

I think option number 2 is better. I have checked both solutions and verified that they both work with the MRP provided by @participant5 

Also confirmed with the MRP from @participant2 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/89101#issuecomment-2461013308
